Converting the armor-shred delta into a post-mitigation damage uplift.

sources_quoted.quote: at which you also heal for {{rd|8%|5%}} of the post-mitigation damage dealt against enemy champions
sources_quoted.used_for: Ruled out the competing hypothesis that the heal itself is damage-proportional: a damage-proportional heal would move the *same direction* as damage (up), while the leaf moved down. Only the missing-health term moves down when damage goes up.

independent_computation.definition_used: overheal = heal_amount - missing_health at the heal timestamp (excess healing above max health). Hence d(overheal) = d(heal_amount) - d(missing_health).

step_1_identity_check.claim: docs/math-foundations.md S3 states the exact Cesaro mean of the capped Black Cleaver stack ramp over h hits is C - C(C-1)/(2h) for h >= C.
step_1_identity_check.derivation: sum_{i=1..h} min(i,C) = C(C+1)/2 + (h-C)C = hC - C(C-1)/2; divide by h => mean = C - C(C-1)/(2h).
step_1_identity_check.result: Identity confirmed exactly. The legacy constant 0.8*C = 4.0 stacks (24% reduction, S1: 6%/stack) is exact only at h = 10 hits; it is biased HIGH for h < 10 and biased LOW for h > 10. Every value stays under the sourced 30% / 5-stack cap (S1), so the corrected model never exceeds the wiki bound.

step_2_direction.reasoning: Roster heals are sourced constants independent of the target's armor (S6), so d(heal_amount) = 0 and d(missing_health) = +15.1: the healed unit had taken 15.1 more damage by the time of healing event #39. More damage taken is exactly what a LARGER average Carve stack count produces, i.e. the h > 10 branch of the Cesaro mean (4.09-4.6 stacks, 24.5%-27.6% reduction) replacing the flat 4.0-stack / 24% constant. A sustained roster fight that reaches a 40th healing event is unambiguously in the h > 10 regime.
step_2_direction.counter_hypothesis_rejected: If the heal were damage-proportional (Conqueror 8%/5% of post-mitigation damage, S7; or lifesteal/omnivamp), the heal would rise with the damage uplift and overheal would rise, not fall. The observed fall is only consistent with the missing-health term moving, i.e. a damage INCREASE against the healed unit with a constant heal.

step_3_magnitude.model: post-mitigation damage scales as m(R) = 100/(100+R) (S5) with R = A*(1 - 0.06*s), A = target armor, s = average Carve stacks.
step_3_magnitude.result: A 0.6%-1.7% damage uplift accumulates to exactly the observed +15.1 missing health once ~870-2650 cumulative damage has landed on the healed unit. For a level-18 coupled roster fight that has already emitted 40 healing events, that cumulative damage is entirely ordinary. Magnitude, sign and the item named in the scenario all agree.

checked: Corrected average stacks 4.09-4.6 < sourced cap of 5 stacks / 30% (S1) -> the new value does not violate the wiki bound.

The Bloodsong amplifier is 8%/5% (S2) and is bounded far below the ~17.2% relative move of this leaf, so the leaf is not explained by an amp double-count; and being a damage-side amp it moves the missing-health term the same way the Cleaver shred does.
overheal remains non-negative and below any plausible sourced heal amount (S6) at both values, so neither value is out of range on its own.

independent_computation.conclusion: The old 88.0 is the value produced by the acknowledged tuning constant (0.8*max_stacks = 24% shred), which S3/S4 label APPROX and exact only at h ~ 10 hits. The new 72.9 is the value produced by the exact Cesaro mean of the sourced 6%-per-stack, 5-stack-capped ramp, which is the identity the engine is supposed to instantiate and which I re-derived and verified numerically above. Sign and magnitude of the observed leaf move both match the corrected model. Verdict: new_value_correct.

limitations: The leaf is a derived quantity 39 events deep inside a coupled multi-participant timeline. Its scenario definition (roster, levels, ranks, keystone, fight window) lives in scripts/ or tests/, which runbook R-18/R-19 forbids this investigator from reading, so an exact closed-form reproduction of 72.9 is not possible from data/ + docs/math-foundations.md alone. What is reproduced here is the formula the change turns on (verified exactly), the sign of the leaf move, and the magnitude window it must fall in.
